1	package strategy
2	
3	import (
4		"context"
5		"fmt"
6		"log/slog"
7		"strings"
8		"time"
9	
10		"github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/checkpoint"
11		"github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/checkpoint/remote"
12		"github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/logging"
13		"github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/settings"
14	
15		"github.com/go-git/go-git/v6/plumbing"
16	)
17	
18	// checkpointRemoteFetchTimeout is the timeout for fetching branches from the checkpoint URL.
19	const checkpointRemoteFetchTimeout = 30 * time.Second
20	
21	// pushSettings holds the resolved push configuration from a single settings load.
22	type pushSettings struct {
23		// remote is the git remote name to use for pushing (the user's push remote).
24		remote string
25		// checkpointURL is the derived URL for pushing checkpoint branches.
26		// When set, checkpoint/trails branches are pushed directly to this URL
27		// instead of the remote name. Empty means use the remote name.
28		checkpointURL string
29		// pushDisabled is true if push_sessions is explicitly set to false.
30		pushDisabled bool
31	}
32	
33	// pushTarget returns the target to use for git push/fetch commands for checkpoint branches.
34	// If a checkpoint URL is configured, returns that; otherwise returns the remote name.
35	func (ps *pushSettings) pushTarget() string {
36		if ps.checkpointURL != "" {
37			return ps.checkpointURL
38		}
39		return ps.remote
40	}
41	
42	// hasCheckpointURL returns true if a dedicated checkpoint URL is configured.
43	func (ps *pushSettings) hasCheckpointURL() bool {
44		return ps.checkpointURL != ""
45	}
46	
47	// resolvePushSettings loads settings once and returns the resolved push config.
48	// If a structured checkpoint_remote is configured (e.g., {"provider": "github", "repo": "org/repo"}):
49	//   - Derives the checkpoint URL from the push remote's protocol (SSH vs HTTPS)
50	//   - Ignores the setting when it looks inherited from an upstream project rather
51	//     than configured by this developer, so a fork contributor's checkpoints are
52	//     not pushed into the upstream's checkpoint repo (see
53	//     remote.checkpointRemoteIsInherited for how ownership is established)
54	//   - If a checkpoint branch doesn't exist locally, attempts to fetch it from the URL
55	//
56	// The push itself handles failures gracefully (doPushRef warns and continues),
57	// so no reachability check is needed here.
58	func resolvePushSettings(ctx context.Context, pushRemoteName string) pushSettings {
59		s, err := settings.Load(ctx)
60		if err != nil {
61			return pushSettings{remote: pushRemoteName}
62		}
63	
64		ps := pushSettings{
65			remote:       pushRemoteName,
66			pushDisabled: s.IsPushSessionsDisabled(),
67		}
68	
69		config := s.GetCheckpointRemote()
70		if config == nil {
71			return ps
72		}
73		checkpointURL, enabled, err := remote.PushURL(ctx, pushRemoteName)
74		if err != nil {
75			logging.Warn(ctx, "checkpoint-remote: could not derive URL from push remote",
76				slog.String("remote", pushRemoteName),
77				slog.String("repo", config.Repo),
78				slog.String("error", err.Error()),
79			)
80			return ps
81		}
82		if !enabled || checkpointURL == "" {
83			return ps
84		}
85	
86		ps.checkpointURL = checkpointURL
87	
88		// If the v1 checkpoint branch doesn't exist locally, try to fetch it from the URL.
89		// This is a one-time operation — once the branch exists locally, subsequent pushes
90		// skip the fetch entirely. Only fetch the metadata branch; trails are always pushed
91		// to the user's push remote, not the checkpoint remote.
92		if err := fetchMetadataBranchIfMissing(ctx, checkpointURL); err != nil {
93			logging.Warn(ctx, "checkpoint-remote: failed to fetch metadata branch",
94				slog.String("error", err.Error()),
95			)
96		}
97	
98		return ps
99	}
100	
101	// FetchMetadataBranch fetches the metadata branch from the checkpoint remote URL
102	// and updates the local branch. Unlike fetchMetadataBranchIfMissing, this always
103	// fetches regardless of whether the branch exists locally (for resume scenarios
104	// where the local branch may be stale).
105	//
106	// The fetch is unfiltered (NoFilter: true) because resume needs blob content
107	// (transcripts, metadata JSON) — not just tree objects.
108	func FetchMetadataBranch(ctx context.Context, remoteURL string) error {
109		refs := checkpoint.ResolveRefs(ctx)
110		if !refs.Primary.IsBranch() {
111			return fmt.Errorf("primary metadata ref %s is not a branch", refs.Primary)
112		}
113		branchName := refs.Primary.Short()
114		tmpRef := FetchTmpRefPrefix + branchName

134	// fetches are globally enabled. Use noFilter for operations that need blob
135	// content (resume, explain) as opposed to sync operations (push recovery)
136	// that only need tree structure.
137	func fetchURLIntoTmpRef(ctx context.Context, dir, remoteURL, srcRef, tmpRef, label string, noFilter bool) error { //nolint:unparam // noFilter distinguishes blob-content fetches (true) from tree-only sync fetches (false); kept for the documented fetch-filtering contract even though current callers all need blob content

139		defer cancel()

145			NoTags:   true,
146			NoFilter: noFilter,
147			Dir:      dir,
148		})
149		if fetchErr == nil {

153		redactedURL := remote.RedactURL(remoteURL)
154		msg := strings.TrimSpace(strings.ReplaceAll(string(output), remoteURL, redactedURL))
155		if msg != "" {

162	// This avoids network calls on every push — once the branch exists locally, this is a no-op.
163	// Fetch failures are silently swallowed (returns nil): the push will handle creating the
164	// branch on the remote. Only fatal errors (opening repo, creating local branch) are returned.
165	func fetchMetadataBranchIfMissing(ctx context.Context, remoteURL string) error {
166		repo, err := OpenRepository(ctx)
167		if err != nil {

169		}

173		refs := checkpoint.ResolveRefs(ctx)

175			return nil // Branch exists locally, skip fetch
176		}

178		// Branch doesn't exist locally - try to fetch it from the URL.
179		// Fetch failures are not fatal: push will create it on the remote when it succeeds.
180		if err := FetchMetadataBranch(ctx, remoteURL); err != nil {

189	// rooted at worktreeRoot and verifies it actually targets the configured
190	// checkpoint repository. It returns ok=false (never an error) when no
191	// checkpoint_remote is configured or a dedicated checkpoint URL cannot be
192	// resolved, so callers fall back to keeping the local branch / creating an orphan.
193	//
194	// remote.FetchURL silently falls back to the origin remote URL in several paths
195	// (ENTIRE_CHECKPOINT_TOKEN short-circuit, unparseable origin, non-derivable origin
196	// protocol). Adopting from origin would contradict the rule that origin is never
197	// authoritative when a checkpoint_remote is configured (issue #1374), so a resolved
198	// URL that does not target the configured checkpoint repo is treated as unresolved.
199	func resolveCheckpointFetchURL(ctx context.Context, worktreeRoot string) (string, bool) {
200		s, err := settings.Load(ctx)

215		}
216		if !urlTargetsCheckpointRepo(url, config) {
217			logging.Debug(ctx, "checkpoint-remote: fetch URL did not resolve to the configured checkpoint repo; not adopting from origin",

220		}
221		return url, true
222	}

225	// repository (host-agnostic, case-insensitive owner/repo match). It distinguishes a
226	// derived checkpoint URL from remote.FetchURL's origin fallback, which targets the
227	// origin repository instead. A same-repo checkpoint_remote (origin == checkpoint
228	// repo) still matches, which is correct: adopting from that URL is adopting the
229	// checkpoint repo.
230	func urlTargetsCheckpointRepo(url string, config *settings.CheckpointRemoteConfig) bool {
231		info, err := remote.ParseURL(url)
232		if err != nil || info.Owner == "" || info.Repo == "" {
233			return false
234		}
235		return strings.EqualFold(info.Owner+"/"+info.Repo, config.Repo)

content.text:
Confirmed, and it's worse than just `enable`. Here's the chain.

## What's happening

A fresh clone of `entireio/cli` ships this **committed** in `.entire/settings.json`:

```json
"checkpoint_remote": { "provider": "github", "repo": "entireio/cli-checkpoints" },
"filtered_fetches": true,
"checkpoints": { "primary": { "type": "git-refs" } }
```

`entire enable` → `EnsureSetup(WithCheckpointRemoteBootstrap)` (`setup.go:1168`) → `EnsurePrimaryRef` → local `entire/checkpoints/v1` is missing → `bootstrapPrimaryFromCheckpointRemote` (`strategy/common.go:673`) → `fetchURLIntoTmpRef(..., noFilter=true)` under a 30s cap (`strategy/checkpoint_remote.go:19,138`).

I ran that exact refspec against the real remote:

```
Receiving objects: 100% (104083/104083), 1.53 GiB | 19.15 MiB/s, done.
```

**1.53 GiB, 104k objects.** ~82s on a 19 MiB/s link — so the 30s deadline can never be met, and on a normal connection you get maybe a fifth of the way in. Note `NoFilter: true` deliberately overrides the repo's own `filtered_fetches: true`, so it's pulling every transcript blob ever written, not just trees.

## Three separate defects

**1. It never converges.** This is why the second run behaves identically. Because the primary backend is `git-refs`, `skipEmptyOrphan` is true (`common.go:498`), so after the failed bootstrap `EnsurePrimaryRef` returns without creating *anything* (`common.go:539-541`). Next `entire enable` sees byte-identical state and re-fetches. On the git-branch backend it would at least seed an orphan and stop; with git-refs it's an unbounded retry.

**2. The failure is logged at Debug.** `common.go:707` — `logging.Debug(ctx, "checkpoint-remote: enable bootstrap fetch failed; creating empty orphan")`. Invisible at default log level, and the message is wrong under git-refs (no orphan gets created).

**3. `git push` pays the same tax, silently.** `resolvePushSettings` (`checkpoint_remote.go:92`) calls `fetchMetadataBranchIfMissing` unconditionally — it is *not* gated on the bootstrap flag — and it's the first thing `prePush` does (`manual_commit_push.go:71`). Its comment claims:

> This is a one-time operation — once the branch exists locally, subsequent pushes skip the fetch entirely.

That invariant is false under `git-refs`: the v1 branch is never created locally, so **every `git push` in a fresh clone stalls up to 30s** on the same 1.5 GiB fetch. It sits outside the 2-minute `checkpointPushBudget`, which only wraps `doPushRef`. And the error is swallowed twice — `fetchMetadataBranchIfMissing` returns `nil` on failure (`checkpoint_remote.go:180-182`), so the `logging.Warn` at line 93 never fires either.

## What I'd fix

- **Skip the v1 fetch entirely when the primary backend is `git-refs`.** Both call sites are chasing a branch this repo never reads or writes. That alone kills the enable stall *and* the per-push stall.
- **Make the remaining fetch cheap.** `--filter=blob:none` (why `noFilter=true` here? bootstrap only needs to establish the ref, not the blobs) and/or `--depth`. A tip-only bootstrap is ~nothing.
- **Don't retry forever.** After a failed bootstrap, record that fact locally so the next `enable` doesn't re-pay 30s.
- **Tell the user.** At minimum a spinner (`Fetching checkpoint history from entireio/cli-checkpoints…`) and, on timeout, one line at Warn: what failed, that it's non-fatal, and how to skip. Right now a fresh contributor gets 30 seconds of dead terminal, twice, with no explanation.

I haven't changed anything — want me to open an issue, or go straight to a fix?

content.text:
Good instinct — I checked, and the answer changes the recommendation. Keep the branch; drop the eager fetch.

## The branch is load-bearing, not vestigial

Measured on `entireio/cli-checkpoints`:

| store | count |
|---|---|
| `entire/checkpoints/v1` branch | **5,390** legacy hex-ID checkpoints (12,918 commits) |
| git-refs backend (`refs/entire/checkpoints/…`) | **721** ULID refs |

And the code already treats it as a first-class read source *under* git-refs primary. `buildKindReadStores` (`checkpoint/open.go:110-125`) builds a git-branch read store alongside the refs store regardless of which is primary, and `newKindRoutingStore` routes id-keyed reads by ID format — hex → branch, ULID → refs. So ~88% of this repo's checkpoint history is only reachable through that branch. Nothing should touch that.

## And yes — it self-heals, more cheaply than the eager fetch

The read paths fetch v1 at the moment a read actually needs it:

- `resume` → `getMetadataTree` (`resume.go:441`) — a full ladder: checkpoint_remote → treeless origin → local → full origin
- `resume` → `checkRemoteMetadata` (`resume.go:787`)
- `explain --export`, `attach` → same `getMetadataTree`

fix(checkpoint): stop eagerly cloning v1 under the git-refs backend

A fresh clone of a repo whose committed settings pair a checkpoint_remote
with the git-refs primary backend stalls on `entire enable`, and again on
every `git push`, while it downloads the entire legacy transcript archive.
On this repo's own checkpoint remote that is 1.53 GiB / 104k objects
against a 30s deadline, so it never completes — and because the git-refs
path deliberately creates no orphan on failure, the next run finds
identical state and starts over. It never converges.

Both call sites fetch v1 for reasons that do not apply to git-refs:

  - bootstrapPrimaryFromCheckpointRemote exists to stop a freshly seeded
    local orphan from diverging from the real branch. Under git-refs no
    orphan is ever seeded (skipEmptyOrphan) and nothing is written to v1,
    so there is no divergence to prevent.

  - fetchMetadataBranchIfMissing is documented as one-time, amortised by
    the branch existing locally afterwards. Under git-refs prePush pushes
    per-checkpoint refs and never creates v1 locally, so the branch stays
    missing forever and the "one-time" cost recurs on every push.

Gate both on the backend. Legacy hex-ID checkpoints stay readable: v1
remains a first-class read source via kind routing, and the read paths
fetch it from the checkpoint remote when a read actually needs it —
by blob hash where possible, rather than the whole branch.
EOF

perf(checkpoint): fetch the enable bootstrap blob-filtered

The enable-time bootstrap and empty-orphan heal both fetched v1 with
NoFilter, pulling every transcript blob ever committed. Neither needs
them: the bootstrap only has to land the ref at the remote tip so a
later orphan cannot diverge from it (SafelyAdvanceLocalRef takes the
ref-not-found path and just sets the hash), and the heal only inspects
the root tree's entry names via metadataBranchHasData.

Since v1's blobs are the whole transcript archive, that turned `entire
enable` on a fresh clone into a full-history download. Drop NoFilter on
both so they honor filtered_fetches like other sync operations; reads
still pull the blobs they need on demand through BlobFetcher.

Repos that have not opted into filtered_fetches are unaffected — the
flag only suppresses an explicit override, it does not force filtering
on a user who did not ask for a partial clone.
